"""
    DataManager

Module for managing data in the velocity field GUI application.
Consists of a struct called VelocityField to hold the data and
functions to load the data, validate the eigenstate string and
calculate the velocity field. It uses a PlotSettings struct to
hold the UI settings.
"""
module DataManager

using HDF5
using Symbolics
using StaticArrays
using Base.Threads

# Import PlotSettings from UISettings
include("UISettings.jl")
using .UISettings: PlotSettings

export VelocityField, load_data, calculate_velocity_field, validate_eigenstate_string, PlotSettings

# File naming conventions - kept as documentation of expected file structure
const EIGENSTATE_INFO_FILE = "eigenstate_info.h5"
const BASIS_FUNCTION_REGISTRY_FILE = "basis_function_registry.h5"
const AMPLITUDES_FILE = "amplitudes.h5"
const TIME_DATA_FILE = "time_data.h5"
const GRID_FILE = "grid.h5"
const REQUIRED_FILES = [
    EIGENSTATE_INFO_FILE,
    BASIS_FUNCTION_REGISTRY_FILE,
    AMPLITUDES_FILE,
    TIME_DATA_FILE,
    GRID_FILE
]

"""
    VelocityField

Structure to hold velocity field data, metadata, file references, and visualization settings.

Fields:
- `data_dir::String`: Directory containing the input files
- `file_paths::Dict{String,String}`: Mapping between file types and their full paths
- `x::Vector{Float64}`: x coordinates
- `y::Vector{Float64}`: y coordinates
- `z::Vector{Float64}`: z coordinates
- `nx::Int`: Number of points in x direction
- `ny::Int`: Number of points in y direction
- `nz::Int`: Number of points in z direction
- `ui_states::PlotSettings`: Current visualization settings
- `ux::Vector{Float64}`: x-component of velocity
- `uy::Vector{Float64}`: y-component of velocity
- `uz::Vector{Float64}`: z-component of velocity
- `amplitudes::Array{Float64, 2}`: Amplitudes of eigenstates at different time steps
- `time_steps::Vector{Float64}`: Time values for the simulation
- `ki::Array{Float64, 2}`: Wave numbers for each eigenstate
- `ai::Array{Float64, 2}`: Eigenvectors for each eigenstate
- `ku::Float64`: Base flow wave number
- `U::Float64`: Base flow amplitude
- `flow_type::String`: Type of flow
- `basis_functions::Dict{String, Function}`: Basis functions for velocity components
- `base_flow::Dict{String, Function}`: Base flow functions for velocity components
"""
@kwdef struct VelocityField
    data_dir::String
    file_paths::Dict{String,String}
    x::Vector{Float64}
    y::Vector{Float64}
    z::Vector{Float64}
    nx::Int
    ny::Int
    nz::Int
    ui_states::PlotSettings = PlotSettings()
    ux::Vector{Float64} = Float64[]
    uy::Vector{Float64} = Float64[]
    uz::Vector{Float64} = Float64[]
    amplitudes::Array{Float64, 2}
    time_steps::Vector{Float64}
    ki::Array{Float64, 2}
    ai::Array{Float64, 2}
    ku::Float64
    U::Float64
    flow_type::String
    basis_functions::Dict{String, Function}
    base_flow::Dict{String, Function}
end

# Pretty printing
Base.show(io::IO, obj::VelocityField) = dump(io, obj; maxdepth=1)

"""
    load_data(data_dir::String) -> VelocityField

Load velocity field data from the specified directory and returns a VelocityField object.
If the directory does not contain the filenames specified in the REQUIRED_FILES array,
an error is thrown.

# Arguments
- `data_dir::String`: Directory containing the input files

# Returns
- `VelocityField`: A VelocityField object containing velocity field data
"""
function load_data(data_dir::String)
    # Check that directory exists
    if !isdir(data_dir)
        throw(ArgumentError("Directory $data_dir does not exist"))
    end

    # Create the file_paths dictionary mapping file types to full paths
    file_paths = Dict{String,String}()

    # Check for required files and store their paths
    for file in REQUIRED_FILES
        file_path = joinpath(data_dir, file)
        if !isfile(file_path)
            throw(ArgumentError("Required file $file not found in $data_dir"))
        end
        file_paths[file] = file_path
    end

    # Load grid data
    x, y, z, nx, ny, nz = _get_grid_data(file_paths[GRID_FILE])

    # Initialize variables for additional data
    flow_type = nothing
    basis_functions = nothing
    base_flow = nothing
    built_basis_functions = nothing
    built_base_flow = nothing
    variables = nothing
    amplitudes = nothing
    time_steps = nothing
    ki = nothing
    ai = nothing
    ku = nothing
    U = nothing

    # Load from eigenstate_info.h5
    h5open(file_paths[EIGENSTATE_INFO_FILE], "r") do file
        ki = read(file["ki"])
        ai = read(file["ai"])
        U = read(file["base_flow"]["U"])
        ku = read(file["base_flow"]["ku"])
        flow_type = read(file["flow_type"])
    end

    # Load from amplitudes.h5
    h5open(file_paths[AMPLITUDES_FILE], "r") do file
        amplitudes = read(file["vel_data"])
    end

    # Load from time_data.h5
    h5open(file_paths[TIME_DATA_FILE], "r") do file
        time_steps = read(file["time_data"])
    end

    # Load from basis_function_registry.h5
    h5open(file_paths[BASIS_FUNCTION_REGISTRY_FILE], "r") do file
        functions = read(file[flow_type])

        # Fetch the basis functions and the base flow
        basis_functions = functions["basis_function"]
        base_flow = functions["base_flow"]

        # Get the variables for the functions and set them in the
        # VelFieldCalc module's namespace and save for later use
        vars = functions["variables"]
        variables = Dict(var => Symbolics.variable(var) for var in vars)

        # Order the variables how we are going to pass them to the functions
        # we build later. This is important as incorrect variable order will result
        # in incorrect function evaluations/calculations
        vars_ordered = ["x", "y", "z", "kx", "ky", "kz", "ax", "ay", "az", "ku", "U"]
        function_vars = [variables[var] for var in vars_ordered]

        # Now parse the equations and build functions for evaluating
        # each basis function and the base flow and store them in dictionaries
        built_basis_functions = Dict{String, Function}()
        built_base_flow = Dict{String, Function}()

        # Convert the basis functions to symbolic expressions
        for (label, expr) in basis_functions
            parsed_expr = Meta.parse(expr)
            symbolic_expr = Symbolics.parse_expr_to_symbolic(parsed_expr, DataManager)
            built_basis_functions[label] = eval(Symbolics.build_function(symbolic_expr, function_vars...; expression=true, wrap_module=false, kwargs=true))
        end

        # Convert the base flow to symbolic expressions
        for (label, expr) in base_flow
            parsed_expr = Meta.parse(expr)
            symbolic_expr = Symbolics.parse_expr_to_symbolic(parsed_expr, DataManager)
            built_base_flow[label] = eval(Symbolics.build_function(symbolic_expr, function_vars...; expression=true, wrap_module=false, kwargs=true))
        end

    end
    # Create and return velocity field
    return VelocityField(
        data_dir = data_dir,
        file_paths = file_paths,
        x = x,
        y = y,
        z = z,
        nx = nx,
        ny = ny,
        nz = nz,
        amplitudes = amplitudes,
        time_steps = time_steps,
        ki = ki,
        ai = ai,
        ku = ku,
        U = U,
        flow_type = flow_type,
        basis_functions = built_basis_functions,
        base_flow = built_base_flow
    )
end

"""
    _get_grid_data(grid_file_path::String) -> Tuple{Vector{Float64}, Vector{Float64}, Vector{Float64}, Int, Int, Int}

Private function to load grid data from file.

# Arguments
- `grid_file_path::String`: Path to the grid file

# Returns
- Tuple containing:
  - x coordinates
  - y coordinates
  - z coordinates
  - nx (number of points in x direction)
  - ny (number of points in y direction)
  - nz (number of points in z direction)
"""
function _get_grid_data(grid_file_path::String)
    h5open(grid_file_path, "r") do file
        coordinates = file["coordinates"]
        x = read(coordinates["x"])
        y = read(coordinates["y"])
        z = read(coordinates["z"])

        nx = read(file["metadata/dimensions/nx"])
        ny = read(file["metadata/dimensions/ny"])
        nz = read(file["metadata/dimensions/nz"])

        return x, y, z, nx, ny, nz
    end
end

"""
    get_num_steps(vf::VelocityField) -> Int

Get the number of time steps in the velocity field data.

# Arguments
- `vf::VelocityField`: The velocity field object

# Returns
- `Int`: The number of time steps
"""
function get_num_steps(vf::VelocityField)
    h5open(vf.file_paths[TIME_DATA_FILE], "r") do file
        # Assuming time steps are stored in a dataset named 'time_data'
        time_steps = read(file["time_data"])
        return length(time_steps)
    end
end

"""
    get_time_data(vf::VelocityField, time_step::Int) -> Float64

Get the time data for a specific time step.

# Arguments
- `vf::VelocityField`: The velocity field object
- `time_step::Int`: The time step to retrieve data for

# Returns
- `Float64`: The time value at the specified step
"""
function get_time_data(vf::VelocityField, time_step::Int)
    h5open(vf.file_paths[TIME_DATA_FILE], "r") do file
        time_steps = read(file["time_data"])
        if time_step < 1 || time_step > length(time_steps)
            throw(ArgumentError("Time step $time_step out of range"))
        end
        return time_steps[time_step]
    end
end

const NUM_EIGENSTATES = Dict{String, Int}()


"""
    get_num_eigenstates(vf::VelocityField) -> Int

Get the number of eigenstates in the amplitudes data.

# Arguments
- `vf::VelocityField`: The velocity field object

# Returns
- `Int`: The number of eigenstates
"""
function get_num_eigenstates(vf::VelocityField)
    get!(NUM_EIGENSTATES, vf.file_paths[AMPLITUDES_FILE]) do
        h5open(vf.file_paths[AMPLITUDES_FILE], "r") do file
            vel_data = read(file["vel_data"])
            # In Julia, the dimensions are preserved as they are in the file
            return size(vel_data, 2)
        end
    end
end

"""
    validate_eigenstate_string(vf::VelocityField, eigenstate_str::String, use_base_flow::Bool) -> Vector{Int}

Validate an eigenstate input string and return a vector of eigenstate values.

# Arguments
- `vf::VelocityField`: The velocity field object
- `eigenstate_str::String`: Comma-separated list of eigenstates, can include ranges (e.g., "1-3,6,98")
- `use_base_flow::Bool`: Whether to include the base flow

# Returns
- `Vector{Int}`: Vector of eigenstate values
"""
function validate_eigenstate_string(vf::VelocityField)

    # Get the eigenstate string and base flow checkbox state from the UI settings
    eigenstate_str = vf.ui_states.eigenstate_components
    use_base_flow = vf.ui_states.base_flow

    # Get the number of eigenstates
    num_eigenstates = get_num_eigenstates(vf)
    eigenstate_values = Int[]

    # Strip the string of whitespace
    eigenstate_str = strip(eigenstate_str)

    # If string is empty and base flow is not checked, return error
    if isempty(eigenstate_str) && !use_base_flow
        throw(ArgumentError("Please enter eigenstate values or select base flow"))
    end

    # If string is empty but base flow is checked, return empty list
    if isempty(eigenstate_str) && use_base_flow
        return eigenstate_values
    end

    # If 'Total' is entered, return all eigenstates
    if lowercase(eigenstate_str) == "total"
        return collect(1:num_eigenstates)
    end

    # Split by comma and process each part
    parts = split(eigenstate_str, ',')

    for part in parts
        part = strip(part)

        # Check if part matches integer format
        if occursin(r"^\d+$", part)
            value = parse(Int, part)
            if value < 1 || value > num_eigenstates
                throw(ArgumentError("Eigenstate values must be between 1 and $num_eigenstates"))
            end
            push!(eigenstate_values, value)

        # Check if part matches range format (e.g., 1-3)
        elseif occursin(r"^\d+-\d+$", part)
            range_parts = split(part, '-')
            start_val = parse(Int, range_parts[1])
            end_val = parse(Int, range_parts[2])

            if start_val > end_val
                throw(ArgumentError("Invalid range: $start_val-$end_val. Start must be less than end."))
            end

            if start_val < 1 || end_val > num_eigenstates
                throw(ArgumentError("Eigenstate values must be between 1 and $num_eigenstates"))
            end

            append!(eigenstate_values, start_val:end_val)

        # If part doesn't match any format, return error
        else
            throw(ArgumentError("Invalid input: $part. Must be an integer, range (e.g., '1-3'), or 'Total'"))
        end
    end

    # Check for duplicates
    if length(eigenstate_values) != length(Set(eigenstate_values))
        throw(ArgumentError("Duplicate eigenstate values are not allowed"))
    end

    # Sort the eigenstate values
    sort!(eigenstate_values)

    return eigenstate_values
end


function apply_fun(funcs::F, point, args) where F<:Tuple
    SVector{3, Float32}(funcs[1](point..., args...), funcs[2](point..., args...), funcs[3](point..., args...))
end

function inner_loop!(u::Vector{SVector{3,Float32}}, eigenstates, eigenstate_amplitudes, ki, ai, basis_functions, xyz, ku, U, i)
    state = eigenstates[i]
    amplitude = eigenstate_amplitudes[i]
    inputs = ((ki[state, 1], ki[state, 2], ki[state, 3], ai[state, 1], ai[state, 2], ai[state, 3], ku, U))
    for j in eachindex(xyz)
        b = apply_fun(basis_functions, xyz[j], inputs)
        u[j] += amplitude .* b
    end
end



function calculate_velocity_field(vf::VelocityField)
    time_step = Int(vf.ui_states.time_step)
    eigenstates = validate_eigenstate_string(vf)
    basis_functions = (vf.basis_functions["u"], vf.basis_functions["v"], vf.basis_functions["w"])
    base_flow = (vf.base_flow["u"], vf.base_flow["v"], vf.base_flow["w"])
    amplitudes = vf.amplitudes
    eigenstate_amplitudes = map(es -> amplitudes[time_step, es], eigenstates)
    ki = vf.ki
    ai = vf.ai
    xyz = SVector{3, Float32}.(vf.x, vf.y, vf.z)
    ku, U = vf.ku, vf.U
    u = fill(SVector{3,Float32}(0, 0, 0), length(xyz))
    for i in eachindex(eigenstates)
        inner_loop!(u, eigenstates, eigenstate_amplitudes, ki, ai, basis_functions, xyz, ku, U, i)
    end

    if vf.ui_states.base_flow
        for (i, point) in enumerate(xyz)
            unew = apply_fun(base_flow, point, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, ku, U))
            u[i] += unew
        end
    end

    ux = [v[1] for v in u]
    uy = [v[2] for v in u]
    uz = [v[3] for v in u]

    return VelocityField(
        data_dir=vf.data_dir,
        file_paths=vf.file_paths,
        x=vf.x,
        y=vf.y,
        z=vf.z,
        nx=vf.nx,
        ny=vf.ny,
        nz=vf.nz,
        ui_states=vf.ui_states,
        ux=ux,
        uy=uy,
        uz=uz,
        amplitudes=vf.amplitudes,
        time_steps=vf.time_steps,
        ki=vf.ki,
        ai=vf.ai,
        ku=vf.ku,
        U=vf.U,
        flow_type=vf.flow_type,
        basis_functions=vf.basis_functions,
        base_flow=vf.base_flow
    )
end




function apply_fun(funcs::Tuple, point, args)
    SVector{3,Float32}(
        funcs[1](point..., args...),
        funcs[2](point..., args...),
        funcs[3](point..., args...)
    )
end

function inner_loop_single_eigenstate!(
    u::Vector{SVector{3,Float32}},
    state::Int,
    amplitude,
    ki, ai,
    basis_functions,
    xyz,
    ku, U,
)
    inputs = (ki[state, 1], ki[state, 2], ki[state, 3],
        ai[state, 1], ai[state, 2], ai[state, 3], ku, U)
    for j in eachindex(xyz)
        b = apply_fun(basis_functions, xyz[j], inputs)
        u[j] += amplitude * b
    end
    return u
end
